status_summary: On 2025-06-12 three Congressional Review Act resolutions became law, each declaring the disapproved EPA action to have no force or effect: Public Law 119-16 (California's Advanced Clean Cars II waiver), Public Law 119-15 (EPA's 2023 decision, 88 FR 20688, on California's heavy-duty standards including Advanced Clean Trucks, airport shuttle and powertrain certification provisions) and Public Law 119-17 (California's Omnibus Low NOx regulation); this reaches the Mandate's goal for California's greenhouse gas vehicle programs by statute rather than by EPA reinterpreting the waiver's scope, and, as an inference, the Low NOx disapproval also reaches a conventional-pollutant program the Mandate would have left within the waiver. EPA's rule effective 2026-04-20 repealed all federal vehicle greenhouse gas standards instead of moving them to DOT, and a law firm summary says EPA maintains that federal preemption of state vehicle greenhouse gas rules continues under Clean Air Act section 209(a) and the Energy Policy and Conservation Act. California and other states are challenging the 2025 disapprovals in California v. United States (N.D. Cal.), where the Ninth Circuit ruled on intervention on 2026-07-21 and no merits ruling was found, and in March 2026 the Justice Department sued the California Air Resources Board, arguing Advanced Clean Cars I is preempted. On 2026-06-12 EPA sent four further California waivers to Congress, including the 2009 greenhouse gas standards and Advanced Clean Cars I; California sued in D.D.C. on 2026-06-22, and on 2026-09-02 that court granted a preliminary injunction barring EPA from further steps to treat those waivers as rules (per law-firm reports), and no congressional vote on them was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-16 (H.J. Res. 88) is approved, disapproving EPA's rule on California's Advanced Clean Cars II standards (90 FR 642, 2025-01-06) and declaring it to have no force or effect.

Public Law 119-15 (H.J. Res. 87) is approved, disapproving EPA's 2023 decision (88 FR 20688, 2023-04-06) on California's heavy-duty warranty and maintenance, Advanced Clean Trucks, zero-emission airport shuttle and zero-emission powertrain certification provisions, and declaring it to have no force or effect.
Public Law 119-17 (H.J. Res. 89) is approved, disapproving EPA's rule on California's Omnibus Low NOx regulation (90 FR 643, 2025-01-06) and declaring it to have no force or effect.

EPA publishes the final rule repealing all federal greenhouse gas standards for light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and engines (effective 2026-04-20); the rule leaves NHTSA's fuel economy program in place. A law firm alert (Butzel) reports that EPA contends federal preemption of state vehicle greenhouse gas rules continues under Clean Air Act section 209(a) and the Energy Policy and Conservation Act.

The Justice Department sues the California Air Resources Board in the Eastern District of California (United States v. CARB, No. 2:26-cv-450), seeking a permanent injunction on the ground that Advanced Clean Cars I is preempted by the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (March 2026 per a law-firm alert; month only, first of month used).

EPA sent four more California vehicle waivers to Congress for review under the Congressional Review Act: the 2009 greenhouse gas standards, Advanced Clean Cars I, the 2022 reinstatement of that waiver, and small off-road engine amendments; a law-firm alert calls the legal use of the Act for waivers contested.

California filed California v. EPA (No. 1:26-cv-2815) in the federal district court in Washington, D.C., seeking declaratory and injunctive relief over EPA's June 2026 waiver submissions, per law-firm alerts.

In California v. United States (challenge to the 2025 Congressional Review Act waiver disapprovals), the Ninth Circuit held in an unpublished memorandum that three trade groups may intervene as of right and remanded permissive intervention for further consideration; no merits ruling is listed.

In California v. EPA (D.D.C.), Judge Howell grants California a preliminary injunction and denies EPA's motion to dismiss, barring EPA from further action to treat the four waiver decisions as rules and directing it to restore the status quo before its 2026-06-12 announcement, per a law-firm article.
